title: Aurora GPU Systems - Redwood Partner Intro
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Aurora GPU Systems to explore reseller/reference partner and joint go-to-market opportunities. Covered product match (hosted vs dedicated vs private), technical constraints (VPC, KMS, SOC2), benchmark needs, and next steps for a pilot and security review.

performance benchmarking: latency and throughput expectations
security/compliance requirements: SOC2, KMS, audit logs

Aurora to send high-level infra diagram and preferred contact for legal/procurement (by 2026-02-06)

Schedule technical deep-dive with Aurora infra team (target week of 2026-02-16)

header: Date: 2026-02-02 15:00 PST | Duration: 52 minutes | Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Luis (Redwood SE), Jared (Redwood Solutions); Priya, Ethan, Marcus, Sofia (Aurora)
transcript:
00:00:05 Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I see folks coming in. Um quick intro, I'm Samira, AE on the partnership team at Redwood. Luis is our SE, Jared helps with integrations.
00:00:18 Priya: Hi all, Priya here, partnerships at Aurora GPU Systems. Thanks for doing this.
00:00:25 Ethan: Ethan, Head of Product. Marcus on infra will join for the deep technical later.
00:00:30 Luis: Great to meet you, brief agenda: partner models, technical fit, security, and next steps. If anything we should add?
00:00:40 Priya: Works for us. We're interested in reseller and joint go-to-market—also curious about any reference customer programs.
00:00:54 Samira: Totally. A lot of our partners sit in two buckets: reseller where you bring customers to Redwood Dedicated or Private, and integration partners where you offer managed hosting with our private control plane. We can do co-marketing too.
00:01:10 Ethan: Quick Q, what's the difference between Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private again? I read the docs but want to confirm.
00:01:18 Jared: Sure, Dedicated is reserved GPU pools managed by us in a shared control plane but dedicated capacity; Private is customer-managed control plane in a VPC or on-prem. Private is for regulated workloads needing customer network.
00:01:33 Marcus: For Private, do you require us to host an appliance or just run in our VPC? Our ops team prefers a minimal footprint.
00:01:40 Luis: Good question. We have both options. For cloud partners you'll run in-customer VPC with our control plane talking over secure endpoints, or for air-gapped customers we provide an on-prem package. The on-prem option has a small management service.
00:01:55 Sofia: From security, does Redwood integrate with KMS/HSM? Keys must stay in our control.
00:02:02 Samira: Yes, KMS integration is supported. We have workflows for customer-managed keys — HSM works for Private. There may be some engineering work depending on the KMS vendor.
00:02:12 Sophia (sic): Sorry, name is Sofia.
00:02:15 Samira: Thanks Sofia.
00:02:18 00:02:18 Priya: What about SOC2/ISO certs? We need our partners to be attested.
00:02:25 Samira: We do have SOC 2 Type II; ISO 27001 is in progress. We can share the security pack. I'll put that in the follow-up.
00:02:33 Ethan: On perf, our customers care about low-latency chat and batch embeddings. What's your latency profile on larger seq lengths?
00:02:45 Luis: Latency depends on several levers: model variant, quantization, batching policies, and hardware. For hosted API we publish perf profiles; for Dedicated we can tune kernel selection and batching. For example on A100-class we typically see 80-200ms per token for llama-like models at 2k seq in optimized paths — rough numbers, we'll need benchmarks against your workload.
00:03:10 Marcus: We're evaluating a mix of H100 and custom Aurora blades. Any challenges with custom hardware?
00:03:18 Jared: We support a variety of kernels and can integrate custom drivers; the main work is validating CUDA/driver stack and kernel availability. We do model compilation and kernel selection step to optimize. We can do an onboarding lab with one of your blades.
00:03:34 Priya: What's the pilot look like from a partner perspective? Do we resell, or do you white-label?
00:03:41 Samira: We have flexible partner terms. Typically for cloud/GPU vendors we do a reference partner agreement: you resell capacity and we provide partner pricing + co-sell credits. For SI partners we have a managed offering. White-label is more limited because of support and compliance; we can discuss on case-by-case basis.
00:03:58 Ethan: Is there an attribution model for leads? We have a channel portal?
00:04:03 Samira: Yes channel portal exists—I'll include the partner portal link. We do lead registration to protect partner-sourced deals.
00:04:12 00:04:12 Marcus: On networking, do you require customers to open ports outbound? Our security team is strict.
00:04:19 Luis: For VPC Private you typically need specific egress to our control plane endpoints; for the on-prem package it's air-gapped so it's different. We can provide exact IP ranges and a config guide.
00:04:32 Sofia: Can you support fine-grained RBAC and SSO?
00:04:36 Samira: Yes SAML SSO and RBAC are supported across Hosted and Private. We'll share the SSO doc.
00:04:45 Priya: Any notable customers in the GPU vendor ecosystem?
00:04:50 Samira: We have a couple of hyperscaler and a few hardware partners but we can't call them out here — we'll include anonymized case studies in the partner pack.
00:04:58 00:05:00 Ethan: Ok let's get more technical — Marcus can run initial bench workloads.
00:05:05 Marcus: Great, what data and test harness do you want?
00:05:08 Luis: We'll propose a benchmark set—short chat, long chat, embeddings batch — with token counts and concurrency targets. We'll provide a script and small sample dataset. We often run throughput tests (tokens/s) and p95 latency.
00:05:23 Marcus: For KV cache and long-context models, any special infra needed?
00:05:28 Jared: You'll need enough memory for model and KV cache; we can tune cache locality and partitioning. If you're running multi-tenant blades we recommend isolating model slices for consistent latencies.
00:05:42 Priya: On billing, if we resell Dedicated capacity, do you provide invoice-level detail for end customers?
00:05:50 Samira: Yes we provide detailed usage reporting and can map to partner account IDs. We also support bulk billing and partner-managed invoicing.
00:06:00 00:06:02 Sofia: Do you log request/response content in your analytics? Our compliance requires no customer data retention.
00:06:09 Luis: We have configurable retention. For Private deployments you control retention; for hosted we have options to not persist customer payloads and to purge logs on demand. We'll include the retention policy doc.
00:06:21 Ethan: Any gotchas with model compatibility — do you support open model formats and quantized weights?
00:06:28 Jared: We support popular formats (pt, ggml/exported formats) and various quantization paths. We also recommend a compatibility check so we can pre-compile and validate kernels for specific quant levels.
00:06:40 Priya: How long does a Dedicated onboarding take? Customer expects 4-6 weeks?
00:06:46 Samira: Typical onboarding for Dedicated is 4-8 weeks depending on networking and compliance checks. Private on-prem can take longer due to procurement.
00:06:55 00:07:00 Marcus: We can carve out a blade for a pilot. What telemetry do you need?
00:07:05 Luis: CPU/GPU utilization, kernel latencies, per-request token timing, and error rates. We'll provide a Grafana dashboard template and hooks for your Prometheus metrics.
00:07:18 Priya: Any reseller margins you can share right now?
00:07:23 Samira: High-level: partner discount tiers depend on commit. I'll avoid hard numbers on the call but will include partner pricing in the follow-up PDF.
00:07:33 Ethan: Security review — we might need your pen-test reports.
00:07:37 Samira: We can share SOC2 and the pen-test summary under NDA. We'll route legal contacts after this.
00:07:45 00:07:48 Priya: Good, we also do workshops with partners — we could do a joint customer workshop.
00:07:52 Samira: Love that. We often do joint workshops during pilots to align product and infra.
00:08:01 Marcus: One minor thing, our ops team runs a custom scheduler—any constraint on container runtimes?
00:08:07 Jared: Not usually, but we validate runtimes during integration. We support containerd and Docker; Kubernetes-based orchestrations are common. We'll capture exact constraints in the integration doc.
00:08:20 00:08:24 Luis: I'll take the lead on the benchmark plan. Samira will own partner program details. Jared will handle integration notes.
00:08:31 Samira: Ok let's talk timeline briefly — pilot kickoff if we sign MSA in two weeks?
00:08:36 Priya: That's reasonable. Procurement might need 1-2 weeks.
00:08:41 Sofia: Legal will want to review data flows.
00:08:44 Samira: We'll get legal contacts exchanged in the follow-up.
00:08:48 00:08:50 Ethan: Any immediate blockers from our side? Marcus: None, just need the test harness.
00:08:56 Samira: We'll send the benchmark template and partner pack.
00:09:02 Priya: Please include a sample SOW for the pilot.
00:09:06 Samira: Will do.
00:09:10 00:09:12 Jared: Quick note: if you plan to surface a white-labeled API, we need to discuss support SLAs — we typically keep 24/7 for enterprise partners.
00:09:22 Priya: Understood.
00:09:25 Samira: Any final questions?
00:09:28 Marcus: Just one — when you say co-sell credits, is that retroactive?
00:09:33 Samira: Credits apply per partner tier and can be applied retroactively for deals closed in the program quarter, we'll detail in the partner doc.
00:09:40 00:09:44 Priya: Good. Thanks everyone. We'll review and get back with legal and infra contacts.
00:09:50 Samira: Thanks — we'll follow up with the docs and the benchmark plan.
00:09:55 00:10:00 Meeting adjourned.

Note: transcription contains occasional misheard words and punctuation inconsistencies typical of automated meeting recordings. Some proper names and product nouns may be slightly off (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" heard instead of "Redwood Dedicated").
